obligation: FSMA Intentional Adulteration rule (food defense)
basis: Part 121 applies to facilities required to register under FD&C Act section 415 (121.1). PLT-07 has been a registered food facility since its plant-based room opened in 2022-03; the other 7 plants make only FSIS-inspected meat products and are exempt from registration under 21 CFR 1.226(g), so Part 121 does not reach them. Not a very small business (121.5(a)) or a small business (121.3), and the 3-year compliance period for other businesses ended before PLT-07's plant-based room opened. Holding at the DCs is exempt (121.5(b)). Confirmed in counsel review; counsel left open whether PLT-07's vulnerability assessment must cover its meat lines

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reporting (proposed 6 CFR Part 226)
basis: Proposed rule only; no final rule was published at intake. As proposed (226.2(a)), the company would be covered because it exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 311612 (1,000 employees; it has about 12,000). Reporting to CISA is voluntary until a final rule takes effect. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System final rule
basis: Applicability is by MTSA facility, vessel or OCS facility status (33 CFR 101.605); no company site is an MTSA-regulated facility under 33 CFR Part 105. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FSIS Sanitation SOP records
basis: All 8 plants are official establishments under federal grants of inspection (Federal Meat Inspection Act). Only the electronic record and integrity provisions are analyzed

obligation: FSIS HACCP systems (monitoring, reassessment, records)
basis: Official establishments with HACCP plans; CCP monitoring runs through plant historians and the cold-chain service, and records are kept in the records platform and, at PLT-08, a legacy application. Only provisions that depend on electronic systems, monitoring or reassessment are analyzed

obligation: FSIS recall notification and recall procedures
basis: Official establishments with written recall procedures; 24-hour notice to FSIS if adulterated or misbranded product entered commerce

obligation: FDA preventive controls record requirements
basis: Registered facility subject to Part 117. The corporate FSQA program owns Part 117; only the record requirements that depend on electronic systems are analyzed

obligation: FDA food facility registration and biennial renewal
basis: PLT-07 registered since 2022-03 and renewed 2024-10; renewal window 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31. The 7 meat-only plants are exempt under 1.226(g). DC-01 and DC-02 registration duties sit with the corporate FSQA program and are outside this analysis

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
basis: Applies to the registrant for FDA-regulated food; FSIS products follow 9 CFR 418.2 instead. 2 PLT-07 staff hold portal access

obligation: FSMA 204 Food Traceability Rule
basis: FSQA records show that no PLT-07 product is on FDA's Food Traceability List; tracked as a pending change in P03

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant (large accelerated filer), not a smaller reporting company. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over the ERP and payroll are tested by the SOX program and are not repeated here

obligation: Hazardous substance release reporting to the National Response Center
basis: Ammonia is a CERCLA hazardous substance with a 100 lb reportable quantity, and each of the 12 refrigeration systems holds about 12,000 to 48,000 lb; a cyber-caused refrigeration upset could cause a reportable release

obligation: Emergency release notification to the LEPC and SERC
basis: Same ammonia systems; site emergency response plans list LEPC and SERC contacts

obligation: OSHA process safety management and EPA risk management program
basis: Each ammonia system exceeds the 10,000 lb threshold quantity in both rules; the programs are owned by the Director of Refrigeration and Process Safety and are context for risk and incident response, not restated here
analyzed_in: PSM and RMP programs; P01; P08

obligation: Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards
basis: Statutory authority lapsed in July 2023. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Protected Critical Infrastructure Information program
basis: The company has never submitted information to DHS under the PCII program

obligation: Federal contract clauses (basic safeguarding, Kaspersky, covered telecommunications)
basis: No federal prime contracts or subcontracts in the contract repository; school and institutional sales go through distributors. Recheck if one is signed

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification; worked example)
basis: The company holds personal information of Florida residents (employees and online customers). Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of other states
citation: Statutes of Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Employees in 6 states and about 140,000 online customers nationwide; notify under the law of each state of residence, using outside counsel's state matrix

obligation: PCI DSS (by contract with the acquirer)
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; acquirer merchant agreement
basis: Hosted payment page for the online store and vendor-managed encrypting terminals in plant employee stores; no card numbers stored or processed on company systems

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons

obligation: Customer agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (assurance reports, notice and record terms)
basis: SL-1 customers receive a SOC 2 report and notice of temperature gaps within 24 hours; SL-2 agreements set specification and record package terms; two national retail customers require a SOC 2 Type 2 report including Confidentiality and Processing Integrity by the end of 2027

obligation: Retail and foodservice customer supply and quality agreements (notice)
basis: About 94% of sales go to grocery, club, foodservice and quick-service customers under supply and quality agreements kept by FSQA

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 with SP 800-82 Rev. 3 for OT
basis: No binding sector-specific federal cybersecurity rule covers the plants' OT; the company's program is aligned to CSF 2.0 for IT and OT
